name: Florida

code.name: Florida Statutes
code.edition: The 2026 Florida Statutes, as Online Sunshine (the Florida Legislature's site) prints it

fl-ch100.citation: Fla. Stat. ch. 100, incl. 100.061 (primary election); whole chapter page

fl-ch102.citation: Fla. Stat. ch. 102, incl. 102.141 (county canvassing board; duties; recounts) and 102.166 (manual recounts of overvotes and undervotes); whole chapter page

fl-103.011.citation: Fla. Stat. 103.011 (electors of President and Vice President)

ties.applies_to: "an office" in a general or special election
ties.steps: a tie in the unofficial returns is a margin of zero, inside the one-half of one percent that triggers an ordered recount (102.141(7)); if the persons still receive an equal and highest number of votes, they draw lots to determine who is elected
ties.who: the tied persons themselves draw lots (the section names no official who conducts it)

sources.quote: In case two or more persons receive an equal and highest number of votes for the same office, such persons shall draw lots to determine who shall be elected to the office.

ties.note: 100.181 says only "an office" and does not name federal, statewide or legislative offices; it is read as covering all of them [inferred]. The recount before the lot is the reader's combination of 100.181 with 102.141(7) (a tie is a margin of zero, which is one-half of a percent or less); no section read says in terms "recount, then draw lots".

ties.applies_to: "an office" in a general or special election, state general law only
ties.steps: same as the rule for statewide offices: the local board orders a recount at a margin of one-half of one percent or less, then equal-and-highest persons draw lots
ties.who: the tied persons themselves draw lots

sources.quote: In case two or more persons receive an equal and highest number of votes for the same office, such persons shall draw lots to determine who shall be elected to the office.

ties.note: 100.181 says "an office" and does not name local offices; read as covering county, municipal and district offices [inferred]. Municipal charters and special acts were not read and may say otherwise. 102.141(7) names "the local board responsible for certifying the election" as the body that orders recounts in races other than federal or multicounty ones.

ties.applies_to: presidential electors, chosen by votes for the President and Vice President candidates
ties.steps: votes for the candidates are counted as votes for the electors; the Department of State certifies as elected the electors of the candidates with the highest number of votes; for a tie, the general rule of 100.181 (draw lots) is read to apply
ties.who: the tied persons draw lots under 100.181 (read, not stated for electors)

sources.quote: Votes cast for the actual candidates for President and Vice President shall be counted as votes cast for the presidential electors supporting such candidates.
In case two or more persons receive an equal and highest number of votes for the same office, such persons shall draw lots to determine who shall be elected to the office.

ties.note: No section read says what a tie in the vote for President and Vice President does. That 100.181 reaches it, and that the tied "persons" are the electors of the tied tickets, is the reader's reading [inferred]. Chapters 100, 102 and section 103.011 were read.

ties.applies_to: any contest in the primary election for nomination of party candidates
ties.steps: a recount is ordered at a margin of one-half of one percent or less (102.141(7), which sets deadlines for a primary election); if two or more candidates still receive an equal and highest number of votes, they draw lots to determine which candidate is nominated
ties.who: the tied candidates themselves draw lots

sources.quote: If two or more candidates receive an equal and highest number of votes for the same office, such candidates shall draw lots to determine which candidate is nominated.

ties.note: The recount step before the lot is the reader's combination with 102.141(7) [inferred]; the lot itself is the statute's words.

ties.applies_to: a measure on the ballot that ends tied
ties.note: Chapters 100 and 102 (the whole chapter pages) were read; neither says what a tie in the vote on a measure does. 102.141(7) and 102.166(1) do apply their recount margins to a measure. Chapter 101 (voting methods and ballots) and the State Constitution were not read, so an absence elsewhere is not excluded.

threshold.percent_of: the votes cast for such office (for a measure: the votes cast on such measure)
threshold.conditions: ordered from the unofficial returns; the Secretary of State orders recounts in federal and state races that are multicounty and in other multicounty races, and the county canvassing board or the local board responsible for certifying the election orders them in all other races; a machine recount (each ballot is put through automatic tabulating equipment)
threshold.in_words: a candidate defeated or eliminated, or a measure approved or rejected, by one-half of one percent or less of the votes cast, makes a recount mandatory

who_may_request: no request: the recount is ordered when the unofficial returns show the margin
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read (102.141, 102.166)
recounts.waiver: a recount need not be ordered for an office if the candidate or candidates defeated or eliminated by one-half of a percent or less request in writing that it not be made (the text gives this waiver for offices, not for measures)

sources.quote: If the unofficial returns reflect that a candidate for any office was defeated or eliminated by one-half of a percent or less of the votes cast for such office [...] or that a measure appearing on the ballot was approved or rejected by one-half of a percent or less of the votes cast on such measure, a recount shall be ordered of the votes cast with respect to such office or measure.

A recount need not be ordered with respect to the returns for any office, however, if the candidate or candidates defeated or eliminated from contention for such office by one-half of a percent or less of the votes cast for such office request in writing that a recount not be made.
no later than 3 p.m. on the 5th day after any primary election and no later than 3 p.m. on the 9th day after any general election in which a recount was ordered by the Secretary of State

recounts.note: "Any office" is read as including federal, statewide, legislative and local offices (the text names the local board explicitly) and, because (7)(c) sets recount deadlines for "any primary election", primary contests too. Florida has no recount on request in the sections read: no section of chapters 100 and 102 lets a candidate or voter ask for one.

threshold.percent_of: the votes cast for such office
threshold.conditions: the Secretary of State orders recounts in federal races that are multicounty
threshold.in_words: a margin of one-half of one percent or less between the tickets makes a recount mandatory

who_may_request: no request: the recount is ordered when the unofficial returns show the margin
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read
recounts.waiver: the defeated candidate may request in writing that no recount be made (the text speaks of a candidate for any office)

sources.quote: Votes cast for the actual candidates for President and Vice President shall be counted as votes cast for the presidential electors supporting such candidates.
The Secretary of State is responsible for ordering recounts in races that are federal or state races that are multicounty and any other multicounty races.

recounts.note: No section read names the presidential race in the recount rule; it is read as an office whose result is the vote for the candidates [inferred].

threshold.percent_of: the votes cast for such office (for a measure: the votes cast on such measure)
threshold.conditions: applies when the second set of unofficial returns (after the machine recount of 102.141) still shows the margin; a manual recount of overvotes and undervotes, by a person, of the ballots or their digital images; not ordered if the number of overvotes and undervotes is fewer than the votes needed to change the outcome
threshold.in_words: after the machine recount, a margin of one-quarter of one percent or less makes a manual recount of overvotes and undervotes mandatory

who_may_request: no request: ordered when the second set of unofficial returns shows the margin
recounts.cost_bearer: not stated in the sections read
recounts.waiver: the defeated candidate or candidates may request in writing that no recount be made; no recount is made when the overvotes and undervotes could not change the outcome

sources.quote: If the second set of unofficial returns pursuant to s. 102.141 indicates that a candidate for any office was defeated or eliminated by one-quarter of a percent or less of the votes cast for such office [...] or that a measure appearing on the ballot was approved or rejected by one-quarter of a percent or less of the votes cast on such measure, a manual recount of the overvotes and undervotes cast in the entire geographic jurisdiction of such office or ballot measure must be ordered unless:

recounts.note: A second stage after the 0.5% machine recount, not a replacement of it. Presidential electors are not named; read as covered like the 0.5% rule [inferred].

notes: Read at the Florida Legislature's Online Sunshine pages: whole chapter pages for chapters 100 and 102, and sections 100.181 and 103.011. Chapters 101 (ballots and voting methods) and 99 (qualifying) and the State Constitution were not read. Election contest (102.168 and after) was not read except to see that it is a separate section. Municipal charters, special acts and local ordinances were not read.

The earlier reader's lead (research/historical-close-races-v2.md 3a and 3b) is borne out for FL: 100.181 and 100.061 draw lots; 102.141(7) at one-half of one percent or less and 102.166(1) at one-quarter of one percent or less. The earlier reader gave no cost rule for FL either; none is stated in 102.141 or 102.166 as read here.
